title: Local Futures: Graphics Localization | Studio 1947
description: How Studio 1947 localised Local Futures' Hindi documentary short, turning motion graphics, infographics and on-screen callouts into Devanagari.
ogDescription: Complete graphics localization for a Hindi documentary short. Motion graphics, infographics and on-screen callouts rebuilt in Devanagari.

hero.alt: Local Futures: Trade Gone Mad documentary

body: When an international non-profit or global think tank looks for a creative partner, they don't just want a translation service. They need designers who understand multilingual visual systems, information design, and cultural localization. The job is to take dense global economic data and turn it into visuals that feel urgent, clear, and native to local communities.

This case study shows how we worked with Local Futures, a pioneer of the international economic localization movement, on complete Graphics Localization for their documentary short: "अंतरराष्ट्रीय व्यापार का पागलपन: Trade Gone Mad".

Local Futures is a globally recognized organization working to renew ecological health and human well-being. They want to move away from corporate globalization toward local, community-led economies. Their educational media reaches policymakers, activists, and grassroots leaders around the world.

sections.subheading: The Problem: When Subtitles Aren't Enough
body: To bring their core message to India's huge Hindi-speaking audience, subtitles at the bottom of the screen were not enough. In fast-paced video, complex infographics, data charts, and on-screen callouts must be read instantly.

If the motion graphics stay in English while subtitles run below, the viewer's attention splits. They try to decode English graphs while reading Hindi at the same time. That friction weakens both the emotional weight and the clarity of the message.

Our job was to audit, take apart, and completely rebuild the video's on-screen graphics in Hindi. The goal was a native, digital-first experience that feels authoritative at once and builds local awareness across Tier-2 and Tier-3 regions of India.

sections.heading: Typography & Visual Localization
body: Translating text inside motion graphics takes real layout discipline. Unlike a static document, video graphics have fixed timings, strict screen safe-zones, and regional scripts that take up more room.
We chose a clean, modern Devanagari sans-serif typeface and used it with strict discipline across all on-screen callouts.

media.alt: Noto Sans Devanagari: typeface weight system

sections.heading: What It Delivered
body: Instead of loose text translations, we gave Local Futures a complete, production-ready localized graphic system: an advocacy asset built to a professional standard.

The finished video bridges the gap between high-level international economic debate and everyday reality on the ground. It helps Local Futures mobilize communities, break down social and environmental divides, and make the case for democratic, local economies across India.
